verdict.root_cause: Platform-automation lowered ad-service's memory limit to 256m about three minutes before onset [tr_066fd3438efe]. The JVM cannot stay resident under that ceiling and is killed shortly after each boot: adservice logs go from normal ad-request serving at 04:36 to at least ten repeated startup banners with backoff-shaped spacing, dying silently with no OOM trace, exception, or SIGTERM [tr_7f31a4dfd996]. With no pod reaching ready, frontend's gRPC client fails against dns:...adservice:9555 with code 14 UNAVAILABLE at name resolution [tr_06e20fa34668], surfacing as frontend's late-onset error spike with a change point at 05:05 [tr_b40dbc22c764]. Frontend changed nothing [tr_f3e14df687d2] and is the reporter, not the cause. The mechanism is adservice exhausting its memory ceiling and being killed for it; the limit edit is how it started, exhaustion is what is happening.
verdict.reasoning: The only proximate change anywhere queried is the 05:03:36 memory-limit reduction on ad-service; no deploy, scale, or DNS change exists for it, and no change at all exists for frontend [tr_066fd3438efe, tr_f3e14df687d2]. adservice was healthy at 04:36 and then enters a sustained crash loop with no in-JVM error and no clean shutdown, which is what an external memory kill looks like from inside the container [tr_7f31a4dfd996]. Frontend's errors all originate in the gRPC client path, target only adservice:9555, and fail at resolution rather than connect or deadline — consistent with an endpoint set emptied by pods that never become ready [tr_06e20fa34668]. The frontend metric shape corroborates timing and partial blast radius: single change point at 05:05, low window mean, ~11% peak, since ads are one call among many [tr_b40dbc22c764]. The artifact did not change and no config value is being misread by the request path; the process dies because it needs more memory than it is allowed, so the class is resource_exhaustion and the fix is restoring the limit.
open_questions: No direct OOM confirmation: container exit codes, OOMKilled events, and adservice memory/heap metrics were never queried; a failing startup probe under a constrained heap fits equally well.
The automation has toggled this limit five times before; whether prior 256m episodes also crash-looped is unknown, and if not, something else changed too.
The adservice log result was truncated mid-window, so an OutOfMemoryError could exist in unreturned lines; Kubernetes endpoint/DNS state was never inspected directly.

alternatives.root_cause: Service discovery for the adservice name broke independently, so frontend cannot resolve a backend that is otherwise fine.
alternatives.why_not: It does not explain the crash loop observed directly in adservice's own logs [tr_7f31a4dfd996]; an unresolvable name is the expected consequence of zero ready pods, and no service/endpoint/DNS change is recorded [tr_066fd3438efe].

alternatives.root_cause: adservice fails to start for an artifact-level reason and the boot loop is unrelated to memory.
alternatives.why_not: No deployment, image, or version event appears in adservice's change log [tr_066fd3438efe], and the same artifact was serving normal traffic minutes earlier [tr_7f31a4dfd996].

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring adservice's prior resource configuration (memory limit back to unset, from the 256m applied at 05:03:36) and recreating the container should end the boot loop. Observable as: (1) in {service="ad-service"} logs, the repeating three-line JVM/OTel startup banner stops recurring and is followed within one boot cycle by "received ad request ... trace_id=" lines, as seen at 04:36-04:37 [tr_7f31a4dfd996]; (2) in {service="frontend"} logs, "14 UNAVAILABLE" errors naming dns:...adservice:9555 cease [tr_06e20fa34668]; (3) frontend's error-ratio series returns toward its baseline mean of ~0.0004 from the incident peak of ~0.11 [tr_b40dbc22c764]. Note the adservice error-ratio series is empty in both windows [tr_f572198ff0f1], so adservice's own recovery must be read from logs, not from that metric.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, more than ~180s after the container is recreated, adservice logs still show fresh startup banners with backoff-shaped spacing and no ad-request serving lines, or frontend continues emitting code 14 against adservice:9555. That would mean the 256m ceiling is not what kills the process — consistent with the unresolved fact that this lower/revert pair has run at least five times before without a recorded crash loop [tr_066fd3438efe], implying a second change or a failing startup probe. Also falsified in a subtler way if adservice recovers but frontend's error ratio does not fall: the frontend metric is aggregated by service_name with no downstream dimension [tr_b40dbc22c764], so it can carry error contributions this action does not address. Before approving, the exit code / OOMKilled event and adservice memory metrics would settle the mechanism directly; they were never queried.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is wrong, this spends the recreate for nothing and adds one more forced restart to a service already crash-looping, extending the ad outage. Removing the memory ceiling lets the JVM's heap grow to whatever the host allows; if the process is genuinely leaking rather than merely over-constrained, the unbounded container can create host-level memory pressure that reaches co-located services rather than staying inside adservice. The change is also likely transient: platform-automation has re-applied this limit five times in 21 hours [tr_066fd3438efe], so it can re-lower to 256m and reopen the incident — the automation itself is not something this action touches, and stopping it is outside what this system may do.
proposal.blast_radius: adservice is recreated, so ad serving is down for the duration of the recreate. frontend is the only caller named in this incident's evidence [tr_06e20fa34668]; it will see connection reset / continued code 14 for that interval, on top of what it already sees. The reverted value is a resource limit, not a dependency address, so no traffic moves to other services. Host-level memory contention is the one path by which cartservice, checkoutservice, productcatalogservice, or recommendationservice could notice.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend plus the load generator simultaneously indicate user-facing failure, not an isolated synthetic-traffic artifact. No open incident covers it, and the fault could lie in any of the five downstream dependencies, so evidence is needed.
